title: Account Exit Investigation Protocol — Renewal Loss
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, repeatable protocol for investigating account exits at renewal (partial or full). Intended for CSMs, AMs, and the CS ops partner who will own the postmortem deliverable. Use this when a customer declines renewal, reduces committed capacity, or otherwise signals they will not continue under existing terms. The goal is to: (1) produce a clear timeline of events, (2) surface the top 3 root causes with evidence, (3) propose 2 counterfactual remediation scenarios with estimated delta impact, and (4) produce a short playbook of actions to avoid recurrence.

How to use this doc (quick start):
1) Owner: the CSM on the account owns the investigation and fills sections A–E within 7 business days of confirmed non-renewal. CS Ops reviews and finalizes the artifact.
2) Evidence-first approach: link tickets, call recordings, demo notes, and usage dashboards inline. If evidence is missing, list attempts to retrieve it.
3) Prioritize: aim to identify the single highest-confidence cause and two plausible secondary causes. Focus on actionability.

Sections to complete (deliverable outline):
A) Executive summary (1–3 sentences)
- Short statement of outcome and top reason.

B) High-level facts (bullet list)
- Customer name / vertical / ACV / contract start / renewal date / key contacts.
- Product modules used and feature surface.
- Renewal type: full, partial, capacity reduction, not renewed.

C) Timeline of key events (chronological, include timestamps and evidence links)
- Example format: YYYY-MM-DD | Event | Owner | Evidence (Ticket/Recording/Slack)
- Add behavioral signals from product (drop in weekly active users, failed jobs, error spikes) within timeframe.

D) Signals and metrics (quantitative)
- Renewal Momentum Score (RMS): a quick computed score (0–100) combining: engagement (30%), usage growth (25%), support interactions severity (20%), feature fit signals (15%), payment/contract friction (10%). Record the inputs used and the RMS value at T-90, T-30, and T-7 days.
- Behavioral Decay indicators: 3-week consecutive drop in active seats, 2x increase in latency errors, drop in feature X adoption to <10% of baseline.
- Financial signals: invoicing disputes, payment delinquency, change in purchase order cadence.

E) Root cause hypotheses (ranked)
- For each hypothesis include: short label, confidence (low/med/high), supporting evidence (tickets, quotes from calls), and required data to validate further.

F) Counterfactuals and Delta Analysis
- For the top hypothesis, propose two counterfactual remediation scenarios that could plausibly have changed the outcome. For each scenario provide: description, estimated Counterfactual Delta (ΔCF) as a qualitative estimate (low/med/high) and a short rationale, estimated cost of remediation (hours and people), and timeline to execute.
- Example: "Dedicated onboarding specialist assigned at T-45" -> ΔCF: high, rationale: enrollment friction was primary; cost: 40 hours CS + 8 hours SDK eng; 6–8 weeks to execute.

G) Recommended playbook (immediate & systemic)
- Immediate (for similar at-risk accounts this quarter): 3 tactical steps with owners and SLAs. E.g., immediate 1:1, targeted training for feature X within 5 business days, temporary credits applied after review.
- Systemic (product/process changes): 2 proposals to reduce recurrence with rough effort estimate (S/M/L) and suggested owner (product, support, billing, SRE).

H) Communication plan (internal and customer-facing)
- Internal: who should receive the postmortem (AE, Sales Manager, Product Lead, VP CS), recommended forum (weekly renewal sync), and whether a skip-level is required.
- Customer-facing: proposed re-engagement sentence, acknowledgement of issue, and ask (permission to run a short pilot, reference customers, pricing flexibility).

I) Follow-up tasks & owners
- Matrix: task | owner | due date | status. Keep items small and time-bound.

Appendix: suggested data pulls and checklists (CS Ops)
- Usage dashboard: daily active processes, token consumption, error rates, and top 10 API endpoints used.
- Support thread exports: last 12 months prioritized by severity.
- Contract artifacts: signed SOW, change orders, billing history, PO exchanges.
- Call transcripts: onboarding calls, feature request calls, renewal negotiation calls.

Investigation heuristics (notes and norms):
- Prefer behavioral evidence over single opinions; cite product telemetry where possible.
- Distinguish between immediate "trigger" (e.g., price increase email) vs root cause (e.g., product fit mismatch).
- Credit recovery bias: if multiple small causes exist, prefer the one that is lowest-effort to fix with reasonable ΔCF.
- When in doubt classify confidence as "medium" and document missing data to resolve.

Example (short, anonymized):
Executive summary: Lost renewal (full) for AtlasCo (fintech). Primary cause: incomplete integration of model outputs into core risk workflow leading to unreliable decisions. RMS at T-30: 28.
Timeline highlights:
- 2024-07-01 | Integration kickoff (AE/CSM) | Notes: integration scope incomplete | Evidence: onboarding-doc-v2
- 2024-08-15 | Support case #6723: inconsistent prediction scores | Owner: Support | Evidence: ticket link
- 2024-09-03 | Monthly business review; customer raised production instability | Owner: CSM | Evidence: MBR slides
Root cause hypotheses:
1) Integration gap (high confidence) — evidence: repeated tickets, demo logs.
2) Pricing mismatch for transaction volume (medium) — evidence: invoice spike in Q2.
Counterfactuals:
- Assign an integration engineer at T-45 (ΔCF: high, cost: medium).
- Offer a temporary discounted transaction tier tied to stability SLA (ΔCF: medium, cost: revenue impact).
Playbook recommendations:
Immediate: assign integration expert within 2 weeks for all accounts with >$50k monthly spend and pending integration tickets.
Systemic: create an "integration readiness" gate in onboarding checklist; product to add health-check webhook for prediction stability (owner: product, effort: S).

Notes / open questions:
- Need direct access to production logs from AtlasCo for deeper root cause (CS Ops action: request data export).
- Confirm whether legal reviewed temporary pricing concession (Sales/Legal).

Why this is different from other templates:
This protocol blends quantitative scoring (RMS) with a disciplined counterfactual delta framework so teams produce prioritized, evidence-backed remediation options that include estimated cost-to-fix. It is intentionally light (7-day turnaround) so we can close the learning loop into QBRs and product/ops backlog quickly.

Owner checklist (to close):
- [ ] Fill sections A–E and tag CS Ops within 7 days
- [ ] Attach evidence links (telemetry, tickets, invoices)
- [ ] Present findings in next Renewal Review meeting
- [ ] Add systemic items to cross-functional backlog with owner and priority

Last updated by: Priya Raman (CSM) — 2024-11-05
